main_text.p: Remota est insita humani ingenii vis, quæ etiam ad recondita Naturæ mysteria penetrare potis est, cui ingens sciendi desiderium accedit.
main_text.head: Ἐξήγησις.[?]
main_text.p: I. Vim hanc natam ad contemplandum & imi-tandum ait Cicero, 2. de natura Deorum. Idem 5.[?] de Finib. ait, Tantum innatum esse omnibus cognitionis amorem & scientiæ, ut nemo dubitare possit, quin ad eas res hominis natura, nullo emolumento invitata rapiatur; quod pluribus rationibus ibidem demonstrat Cicero. Unde & Metaphysicam auspicatur Aristoteles à celebri sententia: πάντες ἀνθρω-ποι τοῦ εἰδέναι ὀρέγονται φύσει: Omnes homines naturâ scire appetunt.

II. Ut igitur desiderium sciendi insitam vim arguit [nec enim natura inesset, nisi medium quoque, quo voti compos fieri posset, præstò esset:] ita vicissim vis insita desiderium arguit, cum ad actionem non in-vitetur, nisi præeunte desiderio & appetitu.

page.notes: Running head and page number are clear. The Greek in paragraph I is set in a small, worn face; the breathings and accents are read as far as the scan allows, and the Greek heading "Ἐξήγησις." is doubtful. The figure "5." after "Idem" is uncertain. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (e.g. "pos-sit", "esset"). The paragraph ending "experi-" continues on the next page.
